themes_detail.label: Dead trees spike in St. George
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints surged to 10 THIS WEEK—a 433% spike above the 1.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting either rapid environmental degradation, storm damage, or a sudden reporting surge worth investigating.
evidence: 10 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.01)
433% increase represents statistically significant spike (high severity classification)
Timing coincides with winter weather conditions; unclear if storm-related or systemic Parks maintenance failure
reporting_angles: On-the-ground canvass of St. George/Stapleton parks to document tree health and identify cause of spike
Interview Parks Dept. on maintenance backlog and whether winter conditions or neglect is driving complaints

themes_detail.label: Lot condition complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints jumped to 8 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 3,100% spike (z-score: 11.72)—indicating a possible environmental hazard, illegal dumping surge, or code enforcement crisis affecting multiple properties.
evidence: 8 lot condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 11.72, highest severity classification)
3,100% spike is among the most extreme anomalies in dataset
Community board has long-standing budget request to 'address illegal conversions and uses of buildings'—suggests chronic enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: FOIA request to DOB and DSNY to identify which lots are generating complaints and their violation histories
Investigate whether illegal dumping, vacant lot conditions, or code violations are concentrated in specific neighborhoods within CD 501
Interview residents and community board members about what triggered the sudden spike this week

themes_detail.label: Park rule violations spike sharply
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violation complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK from a 0.1 weekly baseline (3,100% increase, z-score: 11.72), suggesting either new enforcement activity, organized rule-breaking, or a sudden influx of park usage that warrants investigation.
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72)
3,100% spike is among highest statistical anomalies; timing suggests sudden change in park conditions or usage
Liotti Ikefugi Playground Reconstruction is currently in public review—possible correlation with construction activity or access restrictions
reporting_angles: Identify which park(s) are driving complaints and what specific violations are being reported
Cross-reference with Liotti Ikefugi Playground reconstruction timeline to assess whether project is causing park access or safety issues
Interview Parks enforcement and community members about what rule violations they're observing

themes_detail.label: For-hire vehicle surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 7 LAST WEEK versus a 1.5 weekly average—a 367% spike (z-score: 3.48)—pointing to possible Uber/Lyft congestion, illegal street hailing, or unsafe driving patterns emerging in the district.
evidence: 7 for-hire vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (367% spike, z-score: 3.48)
Community board has long-requested street lighting improvements (DOT capital request)—poor lighting may exacerbate unsafe vehicle behavior
Possible correlation with traffic spike 2 weeks ago (25 complaints vs. 5.1 avg, +388%), suggesting broader congestion/safety issue
reporting_angles: Map where for-hire vehicle complaints are concentrated—are they near transit hubs, commercial areas, or residential blocks?
Interview TLC and residents about whether illegal street hailing, double-parking, or reckless driving is the primary complaint driver
Cross-reference with traffic spike 2 weeks ago to assess whether both are symptoms of same congestion crisis

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO from a 0.1 weekly baseline (3,100% spike, z-score: 11.72), indicating possible street vendor proliferation, illegal vending, or city crackdown that may affect street commerce and foot traffic.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average (3,100% spike, z-score: 11.72)
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago, making it slightly less fresh than this week's lot and park anomalies
No matching community board requests or council constituent cases suggest complaint may be under-escalated by residents
reporting_angles: Determine whether spike reflects increased vendor activity or increased enforcement; FOIA DOE/SBS for vendor license data and enforcement actions in St. George/Stapleton
Identify which streets or commercial corridors are generating complaints and interview vendors about regulatory environment
